title: Settlers Beat and Pepper-Spray Palestinians Near Burqa, Raid Al-Mughayyir and Sinjil in Weekend Wave of Attacks
detail: In a wave of settler attacks across the northern and central West Bank on the night of Saturday, August 15 into Sunday, August 16, 2026, Israeli settlers from a pastoral outpost assaulted three Palestinians in the al-Masoudiya area on the outskirts of Burqa, northwest of Nablus — beating them, spraying them with pepper spray, and damaging their vehicle, according to Diab Hajji, head of the al-Masoudiya Land Defense Committee. Separately near Ramallah, settlers attacked the Shaab al-Louz area on al-Mughayyir's western outskirts, prompting residents to confront them, while other settlers attacked Palestinian vehicles in the Marj Sia plain along the road to Abu Falah; Israeli forces deployed to the area and fired live ammunition while shielding the settlers. A third group of settlers stormed the northern outskirts of Sinjil and released livestock among residents' homes. No injuries were reported in the Mughayyir/Sinjil incidents; no arrests were made in any of the three incidents.

confidenceReason: Reported by Palestinian outlets (WAFA, MEE) without independent Israeli or international confirmation; no casualties requiring hospitalization and no arrests were recorded.

title: Settlers Besiege Beit Imrin Home for Three Hours; IDF Then Storms House, Arrests All Nine Occupants, Blocks Red Crescent
detail: Israeli settlers besieged a Palestinian home on the outskirts of Beit Imrin, northwest of Nablus, for more than three hours on the night of August 16, 2026, blocking both residents and Palestine Red Crescent ambulances from reaching those trapped inside. Israeli occupation forces then arrived and raided the house themselves, detaining all nine Palestinians who had been confined inside and damaging the contents of the home before withdrawing. Soldiers separately blocked Red Crescent crews from the area and confiscated their ambulance keys. Beit Imrin is nominally under full Palestinian civil and security control (Area A/B), underscoring the reach of settler pressure into areas outside direct Israeli military administration.

title: Settlers Pitch Tents for New Illegal Outpost Near Umm Safa, Northwest of Ramallah
detail: Israeli settlers pitched tents in the Wadi Zeytun area near the village of Umm Safa, northwest of Ramallah, on Sunday, August 16, 2026, in an attempt to establish a new illegal settlement outpost — one of several such attempts reported across the West Bank the same week, including near Beit Imrin and in the vicinity of the ongoing Qusra siege. UN data cited alongside the report showed armed Israeli settler groups had carried out nearly 3,000 attacks on Palestinian communities, agricultural land, and property across the occupied West Bank since the start of 2025.

title: Pope Leo XIV Renews Appeal to End Violence Against West Bank Palestinians as Settler Attacks Surge
detail: Pope Leo XIV, speaking Sunday, August 16, 2026 from his residence outside Rome, renewed his call for an end to violence against Palestinian civilians in the West Bank amid the ongoing Qusra siege and a broader surge in settler attacks, including in Taybeh, one of the last remaining Christian villages in the West Bank. 'I renew my appeal for an end to the repeated violence against the Palestinian civilian population in the West Bank,' he said, urging the international community 'to take action so as to advance the two-state solution, for a fair and lasting peace.' The Vatican formally recognized the State of Palestine in 2015.
